facts.fact: Biscuit is Sudhi's pony; Appu, nine, is the groom who loves it.
facts.why: Neela's habit of naming every servant; small texture at Sudhi's arrival.

facts.fact: Devan has known since the second week that Neela keeps a knife under the mattress on her side, and has never moved it.
facts.why: Supports truthful-adversaries beat; consistent with ch15 where he lets her take the knife.

facts.fact: Devan tells Neela that the Keeper of the Passes' office holds one of the three dot-and-split seal boxes, without naming the three keepers; he lists the three seal boxes and Sudhi the palace rider as suspects.
facts.why: Outline requires Devan listing suspects: three council seals and Muthu's rider.

facts.fact: Ittan has written Devan a kind letter every season for six years but has never climbed to Kettamala; the council normally sends a clerk to seal the pass.
facts.why: Makes Ittan's decision to come himself noticeable, supporting the genial-friend-or-knife question.

facts.fact: Neela tells Devan she calls her night-self 'the other one', her first disclosure of the word to anyone.
facts.why: Disclosure ladder (technique 10); reciprocal to his answers.

facts.fact: Devan tells Neela to say the market-day cover for her absence: Parukutty's daughter has a cough (true).
facts.why: Shows responsive care without asking about the jackal call.
